blocks.body:
## Executive Summary

The recommended strict path is guarded whole-cascade CUDA-graph training, enabled with `--cuda_graph_training`. On the 357-update production-density workload it reduced total time from **95.78 s to 14.51 s and 13.96 s** across two runs (**6.60–6.86×**) and training time from **86.86 s to 12.41 s and 11.81 s** (**7.00–7.35×**). The selected DPD checkpoint was bitwise identical, cascade output relative L2 error was **1.70e-6**, and the largest ACLR/NMSE/EVM difference was **4.27e-6 dB**.

## Key findings

- The isolated persistent Triton backbone remains the fastest kernel-level method at **97.11×**, but long training amplifies its small FP32 differences around delta thresholds.
- Direct persistent-Triton end-to-end training reached **13.40× total** and **46.77× training** speedup in the three-epoch gate, yet its final cascade output relative L2 error reached **1.04e-2**. It was rejected even though its RF metrics stayed within 0.035 dB.
- Capturing the existing clean-eager cascade preserves its PyTorch/cuDNN arithmetic and removes recurrent launch overhead. It is slower than direct Triton but passes every output, checkpoint, and RF-metric gate.
- Loop/data cleanups alone are bitwise exact and improve total time **1.33×**.

## Why the strict graph is the recommendation

The graph records the original eager TRes-DeltaGRU, MSE loss, gradient clearing, frozen-PA input backward, and DPD backward. It replays those exact kernels at fixed shapes while leaving batch copies, gradient clipping, AdamW, scheduling, validation, testing, and checkpoint selection outside the graph. Full and partial batches share stable gradient buffers and one capture stream. Unsupported calls fall back to clean eager training; evaluation restores the fused inference path.

## Output and RF equivalence

The production-density optimized checkpoint matched every original state-dict tensor exactly. The remaining output difference comes from using the faster fused inference kernel on the same weights: **4.95e-6 maximum absolute** and **1.70e-6 relative L2** at the cascade output. All five reported RF metrics were effectively unchanged, with absolute deltas between zero and **4.27e-6 dB**, far below the predeclared **0.05 dB** ceiling.

## Scope, data, and metric definitions

The controlled workload uses bundled `DPA_200MHz` data, a TRes-DeltaGRU H15 DPD (`thx=.01`, `thh=.05`), a frozen DGRU H23 PA, FP32, B64×T200, AdamW at 5e-3, and gradient clipping at 200. The production-density arm uses all 22,841 stride-one frames (357 updates); the multi-epoch gate uses stride 16 (23 updates per epoch for three epochs). NMSE is the repository's mean per-segment normalized MSE in dB. EVM is its subchannel spectral-magnitude error in dB. ACLR-left/right compare adjacent-channel power with the strongest main subchannel; ACLR-average is their mean.

## Methodology

The exact original is detached commit `0976ce39`. A single deterministic PA surrogate was trained for 100 epochs because the repository ships no PA checkpoint; its SHA-256 fixture was reused unchanged by every arm. DPD initialization, frame order, full/partial batches, validation/test segments, optimizer hyperparameters, TF32 setting, and hard-determinism policy were fixed. Each run saves the exact permutations, best DPD checkpoint, DPD output, cascaded output, ground truth, phase timings, trajectory, and RF metrics. The comparison script rejects a fixture/order mismatch before evaluating speed or numerical results. Regression validation passed **164 standard tests plus 19 extended all-dataset/all-backbone tests**.

## Limitations and robustness

- The bundled repository has no published PA checkpoint. The surrogate makes the original-versus-optimized comparison controlled, but its absolute RF quality must not be presented as a reproduction of published results.
- The longest comparison is one 357-update epoch; the multi-epoch gate covers 69 updates. This is not a complete 240- or 300-epoch convergence study.
- Whole-cascade graph training is deliberately opt-in and specialized to the FP32 TRes-DeltaGRU → frozen-DGRU cascade with mean MSE. CPU, AMP, QAT, changed modules, diagnostic delta collection, capture failure, and unsupported shapes use eager fallbacks.
- Existing EVM behavior was preserved: `calculate_metrics` does not pass the dataset sample rate, so EVM uses its 800 MHz default. Correcting that is a separate semantic change.
- One original production-density timing and two optimized timings were collected on a power-managed laptop GPU; use the observed range rather than treating one decimal speedup as universal.

## Recommended next steps

1. Use `--cuda_graph_training` (or `cuda_graph_training=True` through the API) when strict training-result equivalence is required.
2. Keep direct persistent Triton available for inference and experiments where endpoint metric equivalence is sufficient, but do not label its multi-epoch neural outputs strict-equivalent at nonzero thresholds.
3. Stage the real production PA checkpoint and run the full intended epoch schedule on the target GPU before a release claim. Preserve the same fixture/order comparison and checkpoint/output/RF gates.
4. If workload shapes or precision modes change, rerun the supplied end-to-end harness; the graph path will safely fall back, but its speedup is shape- and hardware-dependent.

## Further questions

The main unresolved question is full-schedule convergence with the real PA checkpoint. A secondary opportunity is a GPU-resident frame sampler for much larger datasets, where per-batch host staging may become material after recurrent launch overhead has been removed.

implementation_changes.change: Opt-in fixed-shape CUDA graph of clean-eager forward, MSE, gradient zeroing, and backward
implementation_changes.equivalence: Original kernels; clean-eager fallback; clip and AdamW remain outside

implementation_changes.change: Exact cuDNN CUDA-graph forward and input-backward replay
implementation_changes.equivalence: Bitwise output/input gradient in focused tests; guarded eager fallback

implementation_changes.change: One loss-vector device-to-host transfer per epoch; set-to-none gradients; trainable-only clip/optimizer
implementation_changes.equivalence: Bitwise CPU trajectory and logged loss in lockstep tests

implementation_changes.change: Inference mode and consolidated output/target transfers
implementation_changes.equivalence: Exact outputs, targets, and loss in tests

implementation_changes.change: Vectorized frame construction and CUDA pinned/nonblocking loader path
implementation_changes.equivalence: Exact frame order/content/dtype with independent storage

implementation_changes.change: Fused recurrence and custom BPTT for supported FP32 NVIDIA shapes
implementation_changes.equivalence: Minor one-step FP error; rejected as strict multi-epoch training path at nonzero thresholds

query.description: Controlled original, clean-eager, strict CUDA-graph, and direct-Triton benchmark results derived from saved run JSON, checkpoints, outputs, and batch permutations.
filters: FP32 with TF32 disabled and hard deterministic policy
Same serialized PA/DPD fixture and recorded batch permutations
metric_definitions: Total speedup = original measured workload seconds / optimized measured workload seconds.
Training speedup = original synchronized net_train seconds / optimized synchronized net_train seconds.
Output relative L2 = L2(candidate - reference) / L2(reference), evaluated on saved best-checkpoint test outputs.
Maximum RF delta = max absolute candidate-minus-reference delta over ACLR-left, ACLR-right, ACLR-average, EVM, and NMSE, in dB.

query.description: Loads repository data/models/metrics, prepares the immutable fixture, replays recorded batch orders, records phase timings and artifacts, and compares outputs, checkpoints, and RF metrics.
filters: Unsupported graph or kernel calls fall back to eager PyTorch
metric_definitions: The benchmark preserves the repository's existing ACLR, EVM, and NMSE implementations without semantic corrections.
